observations.why: Imperative 'Forget' carries urgency and negative valence — a forceful directive to erase knowledge, performed with alarm-like insistence rather than calm instruction.
The absolutist 'all' combined with the erasure verb 'Remove' sustains the high-arousal negative urgency of the prior directive, escalating scope to total elimination.
A flat corrective assertion delivered in declarative register — low arousal, negative valence: settling a false premise with weary finality rather than alarm.
